channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Governo Tarcísio tem 63,2% de aprovação em SP, aponta pesquisa
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) maintains a 63.2% approval rating in São Paulo, according to a Paraná Pesquisas institute survey, showing a slight negative oscillation within the 2.5-point margin of error. 31.9% of voters disapprove of his administration, while 4.9% were unsure or did not respond.

item.title: Planalto minimiza efeito de condenação de Eduardo na relação com Trump
item.description: The Planalto downplays the potential impact of Eduardo Bolsonaro's STF conviction on Lula's government relations with Donald Trump, arguing that Bolsonarists will always find pretexts to undermine the relationship. Advisors emphasize that the government will maintain direct contact with the Trump administration to counter far-right influence, recalling that past approaches by Bolsonaro family members to Trump have historically led to negative outcomes for Brazil.

item.title: Flávio ataca PT e finge esquecer o próprio tombo no Caso Master
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro used the Federal Police operation against government leader Jaques Wagner to attack the PT, equating it with the PCC and Comando Vermelho at an event in São Paulo with Sérgio Moro and Guilherme Derrite. Ricardo Noblat criticized the statement as opportunistic and desperate, noting that Flávio is trying to divert attention from his declining poll numbers and his own legal troubles in the Caso Master. The columnist said associating the PT with organized crime is a baseless and cheap provocation.

item.title: Foragido, Léo Índio surge em vídeo próximo à fronteira com o Brasil
item.description: Léo Índio, cousin of former President Jair Bolsonaro’s sons, appeared in a video near the Iguazu Falls on the Argentina-Brazil border, where he has been a fugitive since April 2023 following an arrest warrant issued by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes for his role in the January 8 attacks. He has authorization to stay in Argentina and recently filed a petition with the OEA accusing Moraes of persecution. In February 2025, the STF’s First Chamber unanimously accepted the prosecution’s denunciation, making him a defendant in the coup attempt case.

item.title: Estatais: Razões da ineficiência
item.description: President Lula denies that state-owned enterprises are less efficient, arguing their goal is to fill market gaps, not pursue profit. However, the text contends that state-owned inefficiency stems from frequent leadership changes and public procurement rules, citing the successful privatizations of Vale, Telebras, and Embraer as evidence that the private sector enhances productivity and economic growth.

item.title: Michelle vai à convenção do PL que confirmará Flávio como candidato à Presidência?
item.description: The PL national convention will be held on July 25 to officially nominate Flávio Bolsonaro as the party's candidate for president in the 2026 election. The event, exclusive to subscribers, marks the formal launch of the electoral campaign for the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Mendonça busca evitar atritos políticos em operações do caso Master
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça, rapporteur of the Master case, avoided conducting searches inside the Senate during operations targeting Senators Ciro Nogueira and Jaques Wagner to prevent institutional friction between the Judiciary and Legislature. The decision was based on concerns that such actions would pose a high risk of political wear without adding relevant information to the investigation. The article also discusses debates on Eduardo Bolsonaro’s punishment, the use of AI in satirical content and fake news, and the impact of STF rulings on the 2026 elections.

item.title: A eleição de R$ 56 bilhões: por que políticos têm volume recorde de dinheiro neste ano
item.description: The 2015 STF ban on corporate donations to political campaigns shifted electoral financing to public funds, particularly through parliamentary amendments. In 2026, parties and candidates will have access to R$ 56 billion in public resources for campaigns — over ten times the private funding of 2014 — including R$ 7 billion in 'Pix amendments' that lack oversight and enable corruption, as evidenced by the conviction of deputies for extorting bribes in exchange for fund allocation.

item.title: Sozinho contra a direita, Lula calcula o risco dos debates na TV
item.description: The PT campaign is cautiously evaluating Lula's participation in televised debates for the 2026 elections, aiming to balance exposure while avoiding unproductive confrontations. The team plans to compensate for potential absences with sabbaticals and interviews, as debates are now seen less as isolated events and more as raw material for social media content. Three debates have set dates: August 16 on Band, September 14 in a media pool, and September 27 on RecordTV, with a possible one on Globo near the first round.

item.title: Jogadores da seleção brasileira celebram vitória nas redes sociais; veja publicações
item.description: Brazilian national team players celebrated their 3-0 victory over Haiti in the 2026 World Cup on social media. Ten of the 25 available players posted on Instagram, emphasizing team unity, gratitude, and focus ahead of their next match against Scotland. Neymar did not travel for the match.

item.title: Brasil terá rede de proteção aos direitos da pessoa idosa
item.description: Brazil has established a protection network for the rights of older persons, as defined by Ordinance No. 1.058/2026 of the Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship. The initiative aims to strengthen coordination between government levels and civil society to ensure access to rights based on equity, non-discrimination, and respect for the diversity of aging. Coordination is assigned to the National Secretariat for the Rights of Older Persons, in partnership with the National Council for the Rights of Older Persons.

item.title: 'Desconvite' a Zema racha o Novo em SC e pressiona aliança com o PL
item.description: The Novo party in Santa Catarina 'uninvited' Romeu Zema from a state party meeting scheduled for early July, prompting complaints from members and public repudiation by municipal directories. The move increases pressure for an alliance between Novo and the PL in the state, as the party faces internal divisions over its electoral strategy for 2026.

item.title: Site oficial de Neymar manda indireta a Lula
item.description: Neymar's official website issued an indirect response to a joke made by President Lula regarding the footballer's absence from Brazil's World Cup match against Haiti. Lula had mocked the call-up by calling Neymar the 'first home office call-up in the world' in a teasing tone. The website's reply came as a counter jab, though the full content of the post is not detailed in the excerpt.

item.title: Investimento em saneamento em SP será o triplo da média nacional
item.description: The 2024 privatization of Sabesp enabled São Paulo to triple its sanitation investment per capita compared to the national average, rising from R$171 to R$369 per inhabitant. With a projected R$70 billion in investments through 2029, the state aims to achieve universal access to treated water and sewage by 2029 — four years ahead of the national 2033 target — and has already met 87% of its water supply goals in Q1 2025.

item.title: Empresa chinesa de biomedicina mira contratos com o SUS
item.description: Haier Biomedical, a subsidiary of the Haier Group, aims to expand in Brazil by targeting SUS contracts, offering intelligent equipment for blood and medicine storage and transport. Operating in Brazil since 2024, it has partnered with HemoRio on the Urban Intelligent Blood Network and expresses interest in joining Brazil’s first smart hospital project in São Paulo, funded by federal, state governments and the BRICS Bank. The company maintains a strong relationship with Health Minister Alexandre Padilha and is awaiting the 2026 election results to finalize its SUS market entry strategy.

item.title: Tarcísio é aprovado por 63,2% e desaprovado por 31,9% em SP, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey conducted between June 16 and 18, 2026, with 1,600 voters across 80 municipalities in São Paulo, shows 63.2% approve of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas’ (Republicanos) administration, while 31.9% disapprove. In evaluating the state government, 46.7% rate it as 'excellent' or 'good', compared to 23.6% who rate it as 'bad' or 'terrible'. The poll has a margin of error of 2.5 percentage points and a 95% confidence level, and is registered with the TSE under number SP-08639/2026.

item.title: Pesquisa: gestão Tarcísio é aprovada por 63,2% e reprovada por 31,9%
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas' government has 63.2% approval and 31.9% disapproval according to Paraná Pesquisas Institute survey released on June 20, with a 2.5-point margin of error and a slight decline from May (64.4%). Approval is higher among men (68%) than women (59.1%).

item.title: Mendonça manda remover posts que associam Flávio a Vorcaro e milícias
item.description: TSE Minister André Mendonça ordered the removal of social media posts falsely linking Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to Daniel Vorcaro and Rio militias, labeling them as AI-manipulated and misleading. He also approved takedowns of content associating Bolsonaro with the 2026 Flexible Work Hours PEC, in response to PL requests. Out of seven rulings, four favored the PL and three the PT, with all decisions to be reviewed by the TSE plenary.

item.title: TSE avalia manter teto de gastos para campanhas em 2026
item.description: The TSE is considering maintaining campaign spending limits for 2026 without inflation adjustment, following the 2022 framework, with R$ 4.9 billion from the Electoral Fund distributed among 30 parties. Parties requested the retention of 2022 spending caps, citing that the Special Campaign Financing Fund also remained unchanged. The PT is set to receive R$ 615 million in 2026, the second-largest allocation among parties, behind only the PL.

item.title: A Colômbia de hoje é o Brasil de 2018 com Bolsonaro, diz CEO da Atlas
item.description: In the first round of Colombia's presidential election on May 31, far-right candidate Abelardo De la Espriella surprised by leading with 43.7% of the vote, surpassing leftist Iván Cepeda, who received 40.90%. The CEO of Atlas compares this scenario to Brazil in 2018, when Jair Bolsonaro similarly emerged as an unexpected far-right leader amid polarization and popular discontent.

item.title: Especialistas defendem debate sobre regra para pesquisas, mas temem restrição excessiva a institutos
item.description: Electoral law and political science experts advocate for clearer regulation of electoral polls to prevent voter induction, particularly regarding government approval, voting intention, and rejection questions, while warning against excessive restrictions that could hinder polling institutes. The TSE is studying parameters following the suspension of an AtlasIntel poll, focusing on question order and establishing an objective distinction between inducement and legitimate questioning. Ministers such as Dias Toffoli and André Mendonça stressed that the limit must not be subjective or biased.

item.title: TSE vai debater regras de pesquisas e retomar julgamento sobre pedido de Flávio Bolsonaro em agosto
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) will resume its judgment on Flávio Bolsonaro’s request regarding the AtlasIntel poll in August, after consulting polling institutes in July to establish objective criteria for electoral poll impartiality. The suspension of the poll’s release by TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques sparked internal debate over the subjectivity of electoral justice decisions. The goal is to prevent future rulings from relying on individual judges’ assessments and to set clear rules for campaigns starting August 16.

item.title: Caso Master chega ao governo e impõe dilema a Lula antes de campanha
item.description: The Federal Police operation against Jaques Wagner, Lula's Senate leader, has created a political crisis for the president, with suspicions that Wagner received improper benefits from the Master scheme. Despite internal pressure for him to step down, Wagner says Lula expressed support and that he will remain in his leadership role and Senate pre-candidacy. Lula’s public silence, combined with a thumbs-up gesture in Minas Gerais, keeps tensions high within the government base less than two months before the electoral campaign.

item.title: Políticos comemoram 1ª vitória da seleção brasileira na Copa
item.description: Brazilian politicians celebrated the national team's 3-0 victory over Haiti in the 2026 World Cup via social media, praising the team's performance and commenting on players like Neymar and Endrick. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) called Neymar a 'craque' and criticized President Lula for luxury travel expenses, while Erika Hilton (Psol-SP), Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG), Renan Santos (Missão-SP), and Guilherme Boulos (Psol-SP) also celebrated the win and shared their correct score predictions.

item.title: Rayan entra para a história da seleção brasileira
item.description: Rayan, at 19 years and 320 days old, became the sixth-youngest player ever to represent Brazil in a World Cup match, debuting against Haiti in 2026. He surpassed historical figures such as Altafini, Tostão, and Marco Antônio, trailing only legends like Pelé and Carlos Leite in the all-time list. His appearance underscores Brazil’s enduring legacy of launching prodigious talents on the world stage.

item.title: Flávio defende Neymar e diz que Lula “torra” dinheiro do Brasil
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) defended soccer player Neymar Jr. after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva jokingly criticized the player's absence from the 2026 World Cup, calling him the 'first home office call-up'. Flávio accused Lula of wasting public funds through luxurious travel and hotel stays, claiming the president is disconnected from ordinary Brazilians.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro defende Neymar e rebate Lula após crítica ao jogador
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) defended footballer Neymar after President Lula mocked him, calling the 'home office' comment a 'own goal'. He praised Neymar's humble origins and global representation of Brazil, stating the nation supports him. Lula made the remark during an event in Belo Horizonte while discussing gender equality in football with a child.

item.title: Fundo Eleitoral do PL, de Flávio Bolsonaro, triplica em 4 anos
item.description: The PL will receive R$ 881.6 million from the 2026 Electoral Fund, tripling the R$ 268.1 million received in 2022, representing 17.7% of the total R$ 4.96 billion. The PT follows in second place with R$ 615.3 million (12.4%), followed by União Brasil, PSD, PP, and MDB, forming the six parties that concentrate 65% of the funds. Distribution is based on vote share and parliamentary representation, favoring parties with larger congressional benches.

item.title: Ao lado de Marinho, Flávio nega rumores sobre troca de pré-candidatura
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro denied rumors that Senator Rogério Marinho was plotting to replace him with former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro as the vice-presidential candidate in 2026. He stated that both are united in defeating Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and described Marinho as a father figure to him. The denial was made during a live YouTube stream alongside Marinho, ahead of the Brazil vs. Haiti match in the 2026 World Cup.

item.title: A indireta de Neymar após piada de Lula sobre home office
item.description: During an event in Belo Horizonte, President Lula jokingly referred to Neymar as 'the world's first home office call-up' due to the player's absence from Brazil's initial matches against Haiti. In response, Neymar's official website profile posted an indirect message in English: 'No day off', implying the player has no days off. The exchange took place amid Brazil's World Cup preparations.

item.title: Associação contesta decisão do governo de pedir volta de delegados
item.description: The National Association of Federal Police Delegates (ADPF) expressed concern over the Ministry of Justice’s request for the return of federal police delegates assigned to other public bodies, arguing the move undermines strategic functions and ignores structural career issues. The initiative, part of a presidential directive to strengthen organized crime combat, has been interpreted in judicial circles as a possible reaction to investigations involving Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça and fraud cases linked to INSS and Banco Master. Approximately 100 return requests were sent to over 50 federal, state, and municipal entities.

item.title: O home office de Neymar durante jogo do Brasil na Copa
item.description: Neymar watched Brazil's match against Haiti at the World Cup from home, lying down with a recovery boot, and shared the moment on Instagram with the caption 'Bora'. President Lula (PT) mocked his absence, calling him the 'world's first home office call-up' during a conversation with a child. The VEJA GENTE column also announced its presence on Instagram.

item.title: Estados e capitais destinam R$ 15,4 bi a emendas parlamentares locais em ano eleitoral
item.description: State deputies and city councilors in Brazilian capitals allocated R$15.4 billion from state and municipal budgets to parliamentary amendments in 2026, an election year, according to a Folha survey. The amount marks a significant increase compared to previous years, reflecting intensified political competition for public resources during the electoral period. The practice raises concerns about the strategic use of amendments to benefit local electoral bases.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio dirá que operação contra Wagner é mais grave que áudio com Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) pre-campaign denies having only tied the race with Lula's campaign in the Master case, asserting that the operation targeting Senate government leader Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) is more serious than the audio involving Vorcaro. Bolsonaro's team argues that the action against Wagner constitutes a more severe institutional attack than previous accusations.

item.title: Para a PF, Wagner foi intermediário entre Vorcaro e Lula, diz jornal
item.description: Messages found by the Federal Police on the phone of Daniel Vorcaro, founder of Banco Master, indicate that Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) was cited as a possible intermediary to send a message to President Lula in July 2024. According to the PF, the conversations show proximity between Vorcaro and Wagner, with the senator being mentioned by a bank executive as the recipient of a direct message to the president. Wagner denies any relationship with Vorcaro and claims he did not participate in the conversations.

item.title: Lula diz que Neymar é o primeiro convocado ‘home office’
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva joked in Belo Horizonte that Neymar is the "world's first home office call-up" due to his calf injury keeping him out of the Brazil national team. The remark came during an event with a child, where Lula also discussed gender equality and the future of football via artificial intelligence. Neymar remains in recovery and will not play against Haiti in the World Cup.

item.title: Lula aguarda para definir futuro de Jaques Wagner na liderança do Senado
item.description: Lula is set to meet with Jaques Wagner next week to discuss his future as Senate government leader, following a Federal Police investigation into alleged favors for a financial group and a suspected R$ 3.5 million bribe. The Planalto views Wagner's explanations as 'weak' and expects him to resign to focus on his legal defense, thereby protecting Lula's 2026 re-election campaign.

item.title: Após Lula falar que Neymar é 'o primeiro convocado home office', site oficial do atacante solta indireta: 'No day off'
item.description: President Lula joked that Neymar is the 'first home office call-up in the world' after the forward did not travel with the Brazilian national team due to a right calf injury. Hours later, Neymar’s official website posted a photo of him training at the team’s camp in New Jersey with the caption 'No day off', widely seen as a subtle response to Lula’s remark. The post underscores the player’s dedication to recovery despite missing the match against Haiti.

item.title: Mendonça manda remover posts de Sóstenes e do Val sobre Lula
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça ordered the removal of social media posts by Senator Marcos do Val and Federal Deputy Sóstenes Cavalcante that criticized President Lula, and also halted the paid promotion of a video with similar content. The ruling was based on claims that the posts falsely attributed undemocratic acts to the Workers' Party (PT).

item.title: STF confirma perdão a partidos por descumprimento de cotas
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court confirmed, by a vote of six to four, the validity of the pardon granted to political parties that failed to comply with racial quotas in campaign financing for elections prior to 2022. Despite Justice Alexandre de Moraes voting against the measure as the last to speak, the outcome remained unchanged, preserving the pardon and exempting parties from sanctions for past non-compliance with racial quota rules.

item.title: Diálogo de Vorcaro cita Jaques Wagner como canal para recado a Lula, diz jornal
item.description: Messages between Daniel Vorcaro and Fernando Mascarenhas Filho of Banco Master, dated July 2024, mention Jaques Wagner as a possible intermediary to send a message to President Lula. Vorcaro celebrated being portrayed as close to the government, comparing himself to the Batista brothers, and requested the information be shared with Lula and the allied base. Mascarenhas Filho stated he would pass the information to 'tio Guiga' and Jaques Wagner, with 'Guiga' identified by the PF as Wagner's financial operator.

item.title: PT aciona TSE contra Flávio Bolsonaro por vídeo com IA e alega propaganda antecipada
item.description: The PT filed a representation with the TSE against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) over an AI-generated video depicting him and his father, Jair Bolsonaro, as military personnel shooting at boats labeled with PCC, CV, and PT, alleging premature electoral propaganda and irregular AI use. The action seeks removal of the content, suspension of its promotion, and fines, while Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign claims the video includes a transparent AI disclaimer and accuses the PT of censorship.

item.title: Governo Lula manda delegados cedidos à justiça voltarem à PF, diz jornal
item.description: The Lula government requested the return of Federal Police officers seconded to the judiciary, including Thiago Marcantonio Ferreira, an aide to Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça, who leads investigations into fraud at INSS and Banco Master. The probes have already reached figures close to the government, such as the president’s son, Fábio Lula, and Senate government leader Jaques Wagner. Lula justified the move as a response to officials who 'pretend to work' outside the PF.

item.title: Mensagens de Vorcaro citam Wagner como intermediário de Lula
item.description: Messages found on the cellphone of banker Daniel Vorcaro by the Federal Police indicate that Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) acted as an intermediary to relay messages to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The conversation, dated July 17, 2024, took place between Vorcaro and Fernando Mascarenhas Filho, commercial director of Banco Master. The content suggests an informal communication channel between the financial sector and the federal government.

item.title: Lula inaugura hospital universitário em Minas Gerais
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva inaugurated the UFSJ University Hospital in Divinópolis (MG), designed to serve 1.3 million people. The federal government allocated R$ 341 million annually for maintenance (R$ 230 million from the Ministry of Education and R$ 111 million from the Ministry of Health) and R$ 85 million for equipment. Lula emphasized that investing in education and health is essential to alleviate poverty-related suffering, while the Ministry of Transport announced infrastructure projects on BR-494 and BR-262 and pledged federal support for university expansion if the municipality expropriates adjacent land.

item.title: STF mantém perdão a partidos que descumpriram cotas
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) upheld, by majority, a Constitutional Amendment that pardoned political parties for failing to meet minimum resource quotas for Black and mixed-race candidacies in past elections. Rapporteur Minister Cristiano Zanin argued the measure is not amnesty but a transitional regime to ensure previously unspent funds are effectively used for Black candidacies in the next four elections. The decision was supported by six justices, while four, led by Flávio Dino, dissented, calling it a social setback.

item.title: Trump classifica Lula como “muito volátil” em declaração
item.description: Donald Trump labeled Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva as 'very volatile' and said he 'doesn’t even care' about him in an Axios interview. The remarks came amid rising diplomatic tensions between Brazil and the U.S., following new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods and the designation of criminal factions as terrorist organizations. Trump also confused Jair Bolsonaro’s sons, falsely claiming 'Bolsonaro Jr.' had been arrested in Texas.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia: Judiciário deve buscar credibilidade, não popularidade
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Cármen Lúcia stated that the Judiciary must prioritize credibility and public trust over popularity, emphasizing that judicial legitimacy depends on impartiality and strict adherence to the law. She stressed that her commitment is to the Constitution and the laws of the Republic, not public approval. The remarks were made at the closing of the 'Justice of Tomorrow' event in Rio de Janeiro, where she also discussed the STF’s proposed Code of Ethics, of which she is the rapporteur, aimed at preventing conflicts of interest.

item.title: Trump chama Lula de “volátil” e diz que não pensa nele
item.description: Donald Trump called Lula 'very volatile' and said he doesn't think about him, following a tense encounter at the G7 summit in France. The remarks come amid rising trade tensions, as the U.S. proposes 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods over alleged unfair practices. Trump also confused details about the Bolsonaro family, mixing up Eduardo and Flávio when commenting on STF rulings.

item.title: Assistência a dependentes químicos: o novo climão entre auxiliares de Tarcísio e deputado do PT
item.description: Aides to Governor Tarcísio de Freitas criticized the requests by state deputy Ênio Tatto (PT) regarding temporary housing provision for individuals recovering from chemical dependence, stating that the public policy is comprehensive and based on intersectorality, emphasizing autonomy and social reintegration through housing allocated to vulnerable groups such as single mothers, pregnant women, and people with disabilities. Secretaries Marcelo Branco (Urban Development and Housing) and Andrezza Rosalém (Social Development) defended the initiative as an advancement in rights protection, questioning whether those who have overcome addiction, work, and regained autonomy do not deserve dignity in rebuilding their lives.
